verdicts.rationale: All ellipses in the prose are narratively justified. Examples: Farovald's trailing thoughts ('But there was something about him that had changed...'), incomplete questions ('Did the lightning...'), and deliberate pauses in dialogue all reflect character psychology, uncertainty, or measured speech patterns appropriate to the narrative voice and situations.

The prose contains minimal similes and well within reasonable limits. Identifiable similes include 'like flesh that had been pressed,' 'like breathing,' 'like a stone,' and 'like someone else.' These are sparse and integrated naturally into the narrative without excess.

evidence_excerpts: Because it was struck while it was growing. The lightning restructured the cellular architecture. The roots aren't tendons—they're more than that now. They can articulate in ways pine roots shouldn't be able to.
It was three things at once—the lightning, the stone, the fungal networks running through the limestone like veins. They all met at the same moment, and the meeting changed the shape of what we are.
You're going to be its guardian. I can see that already, the way you're attending to it. It will take you decades to understand what that means.
verdicts.rationale: The prose discloses substantially more than the approved 589 storm fragment. The approved fragment is limited to: 'mature Italus in the storm, a human figure in direct contact with the tree, lightning injury, scorched palms, resin/cambium damage, and immediate sensory aftermath.' The candidate text extends far beyond this to include extended dialogue with Farovald explaining causation, cellular restructuring, fungal networks, and explicitly instructing Luca on guardianship roles and duties.

evidence_excerpts: The man was perhaps forty, or perhaps sixty—there was something in his build that made age difficult to read.
I was here when the storm happened. Before you were born, before your father was born.
It will take you decades to understand what that means. The tree will probably outlive you by centuries.
verdicts.rationale: The prose discloses information about Farovald's age and lifespan that violates the restriction. The candidate explicitly discusses his longevity and temporal nature relative to humans and the tree.

evidence_excerpts: You're going to be its guardian.

Long enough that she'll have her own life, her own concerns, and you'll have to convince her that she wants this responsibility. That's the hardest part of guardianship—not the care itself, but the passing of it forward to someone who has to choose to carry it.
verdicts.rationale: The prose directly violates the restriction by calling Luca a guardian and explicitly framing Farovald as establishing a succession authority structure.

The prose does not present Farovald's connection to Italus as telepathy, language, prophecy, or remote vision. The connection is described in terms of sensory perception and biological responsiveness: 'I've changed in ways that let me sense what it's doing.' This avoids the forbidden categories.

The rule text is incomplete ('Farovald's later cover identities and later-book interventions unless the author selects...'). Without the complete rule contract, it cannot be evaluated reliably against the candidate text. The prose does not appear to disclose later identities or interventions, but the rule itself is malformed.

evidence_excerpts: I was here when the storm happened. Before you were born, before your father was born.
verdicts.rationale: The prose discloses information about Farovald's lifespan, explicitly stating he predates Luca and his father by an unknown but substantial amount, implying extended longevity incompatible with normal human lifespan.

evidence_excerpts: You're going to be its guardian.
You'll protect the knowledge of it, carry it forward, pass it to someone else when you're too old to maintain the care yourself.
That's the hardest part of guardianship—not the care itself, but the passing of it forward to someone who has to choose to carry it.
verdicts.rationale: The prose explicitly frames Farovald as establishing the guardian succession lineage and framing the responsibility as passing forward through designated inheritors.

The prose avoids presenting Farovald's connection to Italus as telepathy, language, prophecy, or remote vision. The connection is grounded in sensory awareness and biological coupling: 'I've changed in ways that let me sense what it's doing' and 'the fungal networks running through the limestone like veins.'

evidence_excerpts: The lightning restructured the cellular architecture. The roots aren't tendons—they're more than that now. They can articulate in ways pine roots shouldn't be able to.
It was three things at once—the lightning, the stone, the fungal networks running through the limestone like veins.
You're going to be its guardian. I can see that already, the way you're attending to it. It will take you decades to understand what that means.
verdicts.rationale: The prose violates the story control compliance rule by extending far beyond the approved 589 storm fragment. It should return to Luca's 789 discovery before explaining biological connection details, and Farovald should appear only as 'a reclusive monk who later advises Luca to use prayer as a credible cover story.' The candidate provides extensive exposition on causation, cellular mechanics, fungal networks, and explicit guardianship designation.

The prose executes the required chapter events in planned sequence: Luca's initial discovery of the tree's movement, his period of observation and marking, the appearance of the stranger (Farovald), the storm event, the lightning strike and aftermath, Farovald's revelation and advice, and Luca's acceptance of his role. The sequence is coherent and complete.

The required participants are represented: Luca (protagonist), Farovald (the stranger), Luca's mother, Luca's father, and Luca's sister Elia all appear in appropriate roles. The Leaning Pine (Italus) is the central non-human participant and is fully represented.

The required locations are represented: the north ridge with old pines, the Leaning Pine's position, the limestone heights, the shepherd's trail, the stone house, the rock outcropping/ruins near the spring, and the tree line. All locations are integrated into the narrative appropriately.

The prose maintains a consistent third-person limited POV centered on Luca throughout. There is no head-hopping or unauthorized interior access to other characters' minds. All information is filtered through Luca's observations, thoughts, and inferences. The narrative respects POV boundaries strictly.
